sections.overview: The western capercaillie is a large forest grouse found across northern Eurasia and in mountain forests farther south.
sections.identification: Males are large and dark, with a pale bill and red eye-wattle; females are smaller and more cryptically mottled.
sections.habitat: It favours extensive, open-structured conifer or mixed forest with bilberry-rich undergrowth; in France it is chiefly associated with mountain forests.
sections.diet: Adults eat conifer needles in winter and shift toward buds, leaves and berries in warmer months; chicks initially take invertebrates.
sections.behavior: In spring, males gather at display grounds, where females choose among displaying males.
sections.reproduction: Mating is polygynous: dominant males may father many of the chicks at a lek.
sections.ecology: The bilberry layer supplies food and cover, while young chicks depend on insect prey during their first weeks.
sections.conservation: It is Red-listed in the United Kingdom. French authorities also report declines in parts of France.
